description: An dog hospital has 2000 units of tooth medication to make both small and large bones. A small bone requires 10 units of tooth medication and 12 units of meat. A large bone requires 15 units of tooth medication and 15 units of meat. Since most dogs prefer the small bones, at least 50% of the bones made must be small. In addition, the hospital must make at least 30 large bones. How many of each bone should be made to minimize the amount of meat needed?

TotalToothMedication.definition: Total units of tooth medication available for making bones

ToothMedicationPerSmallBone.definition: Units of tooth medication required to make one small bone

MeatPerSmallBone.definition: Units of meat required to make one small bone

ToothMedicationPerLargeBone.definition: Units of tooth medication required to make one large bone

MeatPerLargeBone.definition: Units of meat required to make one large bone

MinProportionSmallBones.definition: Minimum proportion of bones that must be small

MinLargeBones.definition: Minimum number of large bones to be made

objective.description: "Minimize the total amount of meat used to produce the small and large bones"

constraints.description: 10 * (number of small bones) + 15 * (number of large bones) <= TotalToothMedication
(1 - MinProportionSmallBones) * (number of small bones) - MinProportionSmallBones * (number of large bones) >= 0
